extracted.intended_audience: general_public and policymakers (newspaper readers interested in wartime/post-war policy)
extracted.subtask_description: A newspaper article reporting the National Resources Planning Board's post‑war and social security recommendations, related Senate committee findings on war mobilization and labor, and other wartime news items. It summarizes proposed policy standards for transition from war to peace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of adequate minimum social security benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal government underwrite provision of 'adequate minimum benefits.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reorganize unemployment compensation laws to provide broadened coverage; more nearly adequate payments; benefits to dependents; payments of benefits for at least twenty-six weeks. The board frames this as a central element of a 'cradle-to-grave' security blueprint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal administration and single national unemployment fund
rubrics_metrics.description: Replacement of present Federal-state systems by a wholly Federal administrative organization and a single national fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Move unemployment compensation from a Federal-state patchwork to a single federally administered scheme to broaden coverage and standardize payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of social security coverage to presently exempt classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Extension of social security to some classes now exempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include groups such as the blind and other previously exempt classes; provide benefit payments and Federal aid for qualified persons (including aid for those who desire college training).

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal health program and hospital construction support
rubrics_metrics.description: Aid to local communities to build hospitals as part of a broad health program including government cooperation with the medical profession in a plan for patients to pay medical expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal support/cooperation with medical profession to modernize health infrastructure and devise patient payment plans as part of social services expansion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give Federal security agency Cabinet status
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal security agency should be given the status of an executive department, and the administrator given Cabinet rank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elevate the agency to Cabinet rank to strengthen administration and coordination of social security programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guarantee jobs and training for returning service members
rubrics_metrics.description: Give returned service men an opportunity at education to fit themselves for jobs and 'Guarantee every man released from the armed services a job with fair pay and working conditions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop programs (including education and training) to secure employment for demobilized servicemen and protect civilian war-plant employees losing jobs at conversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal wage/allowance for laid-off civilians and demobilized servicemen
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggestion of a dismissal wage or allowance, possibly paid in installments, as a national safeguard for civilians and possibly applicable to demobilized service men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use dismissal allowances alongside unemployment compensation and public-works projects to bridge gaps in employment during conversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension and liberalization of unemployment compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Extension and liberalization of the unemployment compensation system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broaden coverage, increase adequacy of payments, and combine with public works to fill employment gaps during conversion to peacetime economy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quick post-war sale and conversion of government-owned plants to private operators
rubrics_metrics.description: Quick post-war sale of government-owned plants to private operators willing and able to turn them to peace‑time use swiftly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitate fast conversion to peacetime production by disposing of government plants to competent private operators; pair with a 'conversion reserve' tax provision to aid transition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax law provision for a post‑war 'conversion reserve'
rubrics_metrics.description: Immediate provision in the Federal tax laws for establishment of a post-war 'conversion reserve' for use by war industries for a short period following termination of their war contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow tax mechanisms to smooth industry transition from war production to peacetime manufacture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain graduated tax structure and broaden tax base with emphasis on individual income tax
rubrics_metrics.description: Retention of graduated tax structure and broadened tax base, with major emphasis on the individual income tax and less reliance on the corporate income tax; sharp reduction in consumption taxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tax policy (broadened base, graduated rates, lower consumption taxes) to finance public programs and stabilize the economy after the war.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public improvement projects and expansion of welfare expenditures
rubrics_metrics.description: Adequate program of public improvement projects; expansion of public welfare expenditures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use public works and welfare spending to promote employment and social security in the transition period.

rubrics_metrics.name: International collaboration to promote employment and world trade
rubrics_metrics.description: International collaboration to pursue internal policies designed to promote active employment and to implement ways to open outlets for foreign investments, to promote world trade and to promote effective worldwide use of productive resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate international economic policy to absorb production, promote exports, and use global productive capacity post-war.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation and modernization of transportation systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Railroads be consolidated into a limited number of regional systems; highway transportation be established on a modern and efficient basis with emphasis on provision of express highways and off‑street parking; develop airways for both freight and passenger service and coordinate expanded air transport with other types of transport.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design a rational transportation program immediately after the war focusing on regional railroad consolidation, urban highway planning, and integrated air transport.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention and selective reversal of wartime controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuation of some war-time restrictions so long as potential demand greatly exceeds available supply; consumer goods rationing probably will continue after the war (durable goods may be rationed longer); price controls likely retained for certain commodities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that some rationing and price controls may be necessary in the short transition to spread supplies fairly and avoid runaway inflation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continue some war contracts for maintenance and production of improved military equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuation of some war contracts needed for maintenance and developmental production of improved military equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain selected contracts to preserve essential production capacity and allow necessary R&D and maintenance while converting other facilities to peacetime uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government-private partnership in key industries
rubrics_metrics.description: Government-private partnership in some plants and facilities — particularly in fields such as shipbuilding, aluminum and aircraft — including use of mixed incorporations and granting or insurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mixed public-private arrangements where national interest and rapid conversion require continued public involvement or guarantees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal assistance for private research with open access safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: Assistance for research to private activity, with free access to the use of materials and processes 'unhampered by misuse of the patent system.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support private-sector research while ensuring access to key materials/processes and guarding against patent abuses that would impede public benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use public-works projects to fill employment gaps during conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: Use projects for public works to fill in any gap in employment during the transition period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place government orders for new major development projects (urban reconstruction, river-basin development, agricultural rehabilitation, transportation modernization) to sustain employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vigorous enforcement of protective labor legislation and labor's role in management
rubrics_metrics.description: Vigorous enforcement of protective labor legislation will be necessary; give labor 'responsibility in organization and sharing in management.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict enforcement of labor protections during conversion to prevent undermining of standards; involve labor in organizational decisions to stabilize workforce relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce absenteeism and secure cooperation of labor and employers
rubrics_metrics.description: Secure the cooperation of labor and employers to overcome absenteeism, to discipline where necessary, to isolate and identify occasional shirkers, and to recognize and praise steady attendance and effective work of the majority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid single-cause cures; use plant-specific measures, adjustment of legitimate causes, praise/recognition, and isolation of chronic offenders; discourage absenteeism without resorting hastily to discharges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralize planning and authority to correct wartime administrative weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Correct weaknesses like inadequate overall planning and conflicting authority within government agencies by centralizing authority in a few officials (hinting perhaps at a war cabinet) and improving materials allocation and coordination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create clearer lines of responsibility and stronger centralized planning bodies to prevent inter-agency bickering and overlapping jurisdiction that hamper production and policy execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustain and increase production capacity to outproduce the enemy
rubrics_metrics.description: Achieve production levels (e.g., massive aircraft and ship output) that the enemy cannot equal; maintain high rates of output and transportation of material to theaters of action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain and expand industrial output as a core national-security objective; logistical capacity to move material is critical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social services for families and children (e.g., free school lunches, nursery care)
rubrics_metrics.description: Support measures such as free lunches for school children and grants to states for nursery schools and child care to help employed mothers and maintain workforce stability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in child-care and school nutrition programs to enable higher female labor participation and support families of servicemen.
